title: Hypothesis-driven quarterly roadmap: sprint funnels for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Establish a hypothesis-driven quarterly roadmap that maps Hosted API + Model Catalog OKRs to discrete sprint "funnels" (experiment lanes) with clear metrics, canary gating, and contingency hedges.

Background: Over the past year the team has used feature-first roadmap artifacts for model onboarding and capacity planning. That approach has often left downstream engineering with ambiguous signals (what to measure) and no clear gating for quality vs cost trade-offs. This ticket defines a repeatable playbook to convert OKRs into prioritized experiment lanes (sprint funnels) that include hypothesis cards, metric targets, automated canary gates, and rollback/fallback policies across Hosted API and Model Catalog changes.

Scope:
- Product: mapping OKRs (latency SLOs, cost/unit reduction, uptime, model quality) to 4 canonical experiment lanes: Performance, Cost, Safety/Quality, and Rollout Reliability.
- Model Catalog: define per-model hypothesis card template (input distributions, target datasets, eval prompts, cost delta thresholds).
- Hosted API: define traffic steering policy for canaries, traffic ramps, and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants.
- Outcomes: canary gating matrix, templated hypothesis cards in Confluence/Drive, a prioritized sprint funnel for Q2 that yields 3 measurable experiments.

Approach: adopt a lightweight experiments cadence where each sprint-funnel contains 1 primary hypothesis, 2 supporting probes, and a rollback policy. Coordinate with Eng for capacity hedges (Reserved vs burst), and with Reliability for SLO measurement hooks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Granularity vs speed: small, fast experiments reduce risk but may not exercise tail-latency patterns; plan to include a single wide-tail probe per funnel.
- Cost vs coverage: cost-lowering quantization experiments will be gated by quality regression thresholds measured by held-out eval prompts.

Deliverables:
- Hypothesis card template (Drive link)
- Canary gating matrix (pass/fail rules + metrics)
- Q2 sprint funnel backlog (3 prioritized experiments)
- Stakeholder signoff and a runbook for automatic rollback

Risk: Medium. Key risk is incomplete eval coverage for new model variants which could yield silent regressions. Mitigation: require at least one eval set that mimics customer prompts before traffic ramp.
acceptance_criteria: Each Hosted API + Model Catalog OKR mapped to at least one experiment lane
Hypothesis card template published in Drive with fields for success metric and rollback criteria
Canary gating matrix approved by Reliability and Eng (documented in Confluence)
Q2 sprint-funnel backlog contains 3 experiments with estimates and owners
Stakeholder signoff recorded (Product, Eng, Reliability, Solutions)
